Berezna Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Berezna's Jewish community numbered 1,357 (13 percent) by 1897, led from 1901 to 1926 by Rabbi Shneur-Zalman Gorelik, who later moved to Snovsk. Pogroms in October 1881 left 10 wounded and robbed 200 Jewish families; further pillaging came from Petliura's forces in 1919. On the first day of the German occupation, Einsatzgruppe 7B killed 8 Jews, and 10 more, mostly elderly, were killed that November 5 — among them schoolteacher Serafima Halyavko, killed alongside three children aged 3 to 8. Nearly 60 Jews were killed in Berezna during the Holocaust, accounting for 90 percent of all local murder victims; postwar, they were reburied in a single mass grave at the Orthodox cemetery.
